thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Lower as Apple, Trade War Tensions Weigh on Sentiment

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Lower as Apple, Trade War Tensions Weigh on Sentiment
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Friday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -1.6%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -2.6%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.9%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): +6.3%
ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ): +8.0%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 2.6%.
US stocks were lower at session's half after the Trump Administration said it will use new tactics to counter intellectual property theft by China and as shares of tech giant Apple (AAPL) declined.
President Donald Trump reportedly told aides he was able to get a better deal from Canada after threatening levies on cars made in Canada, according to Axios. He reportedly views threats of auto tariffs as his "best leverage" over negotiating partners.
Apple shares slipped lower after one of the suppliers of its components for the latest iPhones lowered its earnings and revenue forecasts for its current fiscal quarter.
No economic releases were scheduled for Monday due to the observance of Veteran's Day in the US.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 3.1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 4.5% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 3.9%.
Apple (AAPL) shares dropped more than 4% after Lumentum (LITE), which makes components for the company's latest iPhones, lowered its earnings and revenue forecasts for its current fiscal quarter. The company said it anticipates non-GAAP earnings from $1.15 to $1.34 in the second quarter, down from its previous guidance of a range from $1.60 to $1.75. The average estimate of 14 analysts polled by Capital IQ was for EPS of $1.67. Lumentum sees second-quarter revenue from $335 million to $355 million, down from prior guidance of $405 million to $430 million. The Street view is for $420.5 million. LTE shares were down more than 30%.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs (XLF) was down 1.5%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 3.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 3.6%.
Goldman Sachs Group (GS) fell 7% to the lowest in about two years after Malaysian Finance Minister Lim Guan Eng said in a radio interview that the government wants a refund of the fees paid to the investment bank for work with Malaysian state fund 1MDB, according to reports. The minister made the comments in an interview on radio station BFM, reports said. Goldman Sachs is embroiled in the 1MDB scandal for helping the fund raise $6.5 billion, according to Bloomberg News. 1MDB is under investigation in several countries, amid allegations of wrongdoing, including money laundering, according to Bloomberg.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) was down 1.6%; iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), and Vanguard Industrials (VIS) were also in negative territory.
General Electric (GE) fell 6% after Chief Executive Larry Culp said on CNBC that the stock's decline has highlighted the need to reduce leverage. The company's deleveraging options are the IPO of its health care business, the divestment of its transportation business and its upcoming exit from the Baker Hughes oil field services business, Culp said.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 1% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 1.3%.
MagneGas (MNGA) rose some 15% after it said it generated sales of nearly $1.1 million in October, a 180% increase from the $370,000 in sales registered during the same month last year. The company attributed the sales growth to its expansion into California, Texas and Louisiana through six acquisitions made in 2018.
Commodities
Crude was down 1.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up marginally. Natural gas was down 0.4% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 1.9%.
Gold was down 0.4%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.6%. Silver was down 1.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.93%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.02% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were higher.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 1.5% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were lower.
Acorn International (ATV) rose more than 7% after it reported that its 11.11 Singles Day e-commerce performance for its Babaka brand exceeded Gross Revenue (before taxes and returns) of RMB 8.5 million ($1.2 million) in the first two hours of shopping and ended the day at about RMB13.6 million up from RMB7.8 million for the full day last year, an increase of 74.4% year over year. The company's new product category entrant Acorn Fresh, selling frozen seafood to Chinese consumers, also performed well on its inaugural 11.11 selling day, and other parts of the business also had a strong day of sales.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 1.3% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 3.1%.
Matinas BioPharma Holdings, Inc. (MTNB) shares plunged more than 21% intraday after the company reported Q3 contract research revenue slumped to zero from $44,906 a year ago. The company reported a GAAP loss of $0.03 per diluted share, narrower than the $0.04 per share loss recorded a year ago, according to a statement.
